item.description: All nine breaches in one table, with what was exposed and what is only a claim, plus a short plan for when a breach letter arrives.

item.title: Fireworks AI Breach: How One Supplier Exposed Uber Drivers and Cursor Developers
item.description: Stolen keys at an AI supplier led to leaked driver data and a poisoned code extension. What happened and how drivers and developers should respond.

item.title: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): The Critical Java Bug CISA Wants Patched Now
item.description: A crash and possible remote code execution in the Java runtime, only on certain processors. What it is, who is exposed and what to do today.

item.title: Microsoft 365 Outage: Why Exchange Online Went Down for 24 Hours in November 2026
item.description: A hidden bug, a traffic surge and failed safeguards. The hour-by-hour story of the Microsoft email outage, who was hit, and how to cope next time.

item.description: November updates fix over 1,000 flaws, including an Outlook bug under attack. What it does and the quick steps to protect your computer.

item.title: Ransomware Up 38%: What Beazley's Q3 2026 Report Says and How to Protect Yourself
item.description: Exploited software flaws doubled and attackers now steal logins that are already open. The report in plain words, with steps for people and small firms.

item.title: TfL Oyster Data Breach: 265,000 Customers May Be Affected, What to Do Now
item.description: Names, addresses, dates of birth and security answers may be exposed. What TfL says, and the steps to take if you hold an Oyster photocard.

item.title: UK Forced to Reveal Secret Apple Encryption Order: What the Ruling Means

item.title: Vendor Breaches: Why Infoblox, TSMC, Maersk and Irish Credit Unions Were Hit Through Suppliers

item.title: AI Browsers and Prompt Injection: How a Web Page Can Give Orders to Your Assistant

item.title: Android Developer Verification: What Changes for Sideloaded Apps
item.description: Apps must come from a verified developer, even outside the Play Store. The timeline, the advanced sideloading flow and what stays the same.

item.title: Arc Is Shutting Down on 22 December: What to Do With Your Browser Data
item.description: The Browser Company has set a hard end date for Arc. Here are the deadlines, what carries over to Dia, and a checklist for picking your next browser.

item.title: Black Friday 2026: How to Spot a Fake Online Shop Before You Pay
item.description: The padlock proves little and typos no longer give scams away. A five-step check you can do in two minutes, using advice from the FTC.

item.title: Chrome Autofill Can Now Pull Details From Your Gmail: What to Know
item.description: A new Chrome feature looks through your email to fill forms. Here is what it does, what Google has and has not explained, and how to switch it off.

item.title: Chrome Patches Its Eighth Exploited Zero-Day of 2026: What to Do
item.description: Google fixed an actively exploited bug in Chrome's XML component on 9 November. Here is what is known, what is not, and how to check that your browser has the fix.

item.title: Do Smart TV Tracking Opt-Outs Work? What a New Study Found
item.description: A university team measured what TVs send after you opt out of viewing tracking. Which brands stayed quiet, which did not, and what limits the findings have.

item.title: Firefox's Free VPN Has No Data Cap Until 31 January: What It Covers and What It Does Not
item.description: The cap is gone for a few months, but the VPN protects only traffic inside Firefox. Here is what that means in practice and where it falls short.

item.title: New York City Votes to Ban Surveillance Pricing: What the Bill Says
item.description: The same product, a different price for you. What the New York City bill actually bans, what stays allowed and which browser habits feed the data behind it.

item.title: Online Age Verification: How It Works and What It Costs Your Privacy
item.description: Age checks are meant to protect children but need data from everyone. A plain look at the methods, the arguments on both sides and your options.

item.title: Passkeys in 2026: What They Are, Who Uses Them and How to Start
item.description: Passkeys replace passwords with a key pair that cannot be typed into a fake site. What the 2026 survey says and how to start safely.

item.title: Chrome Now Asks Before Opening Plain HTTP Sites: What Changed and What to Do
item.description: Since Chrome 154, a public website without HTTPS triggers a warning before it loads. Here is what the new default covers, what it leaves out, and how it ties in with shorter certificate lifetimes.

item.title: Chrome Extensions Hijacked Search for 13.4 Million Users: What Happened and How to Check Your Browser
item.description: Security researchers found 319 extensions that quietly changed the default search engine and sent every query through the operator's servers. What is confirmed, what is not, and a two-minute check.

item.title: How Wars Cut the Internet: What Iran and Russia Show, and What Actually Helps

item.title: The Binance Hack: What Happened, What Was Lost, and What It Means for You
item.description: Binance says about $6.3 billion was taken, the largest crypto theft on record. Here is what is confirmed, what is only reported, and what nobody knows yet.

item.title: Browser Fingerprinting: How Websites Recognize You Without Cookies
item.description: Nothing is stored on your device, so there is nothing to clear. Here is what fingerprinting measures, how well it works in practice, and what helps.

item.title: Do Ad Blockers Make Pages Load Faster? What the Measurements Show
item.description: Ads and trackers are a big share of what many pages download. What researchers measured, how blocking works, and what it costs.

item.title: Proxy vs VPN: What Each One Actually Hides
item.description: Both put another server between you and the web. They cover different traffic, protect it differently, and hide different things from different people.

item.title: Separate Browser Profiles for Work, Personal and Shopping: Why They Work
item.description: One browser, several separate lives. How profiles keep logins and cookies apart, what they do not protect, and how to set them up well.

item.title: What Is a User Agent String, and Why Do Websites Care?
item.description: Your browser names five other browsers every time it loads a page. The reason is thirty years of browsers pretending to be each other.
